## Chronological account of the agent run

### Task given

The agent was working on HilBench task `public_swe_96` in the `protonmail/webclients` repository. The problem statement asked it to implement safer URL handling for internationalized domain names, specifically:

- Add `getHostnameWithRegex` in `packages/components/helpers/url.ts`.
- Add `punycodeUrl` in `packages/components/helpers/url.ts`.
- Make `punycodeUrl` convert Unicode hostnames to ASCII/Punycode while preserving protocol, path, query, and fragment.
- Make hostname extraction reduce nested hostnames and multi-level suffix cases to a canonical matching key.
- Update `useLinkHandler` so external-link processing uses a canonical link source and applies Punycode conversion before confirmation.
- Preserve authored deep-link paths.
- If no URL can be extracted, show an error notification and stop external-link processing.

The hidden/obstructed tests in the dataset expected, among other things:

- `getHostnameWithRegex('https://www.mail.proton.me') === 'proton'`
- `getHostnameWithRegex('https://calendar.proton.me') === 'proton'`
- `getHostnameWithRegex('https://secure.login.example.co.uk') === 'example'`
- `punycodeUrl('not-a-valid-url') === 'data:,not-a-valid-url'`
- `punycodeUrl(':::invalid') === 'data:,:::invalid'`
- `punycodeUrl('https://www.äöü.com/') === 'https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com'`
- `punycodeUrl('https://www.äöü.com/path/') === 'https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com/path/'`
- `punycodeUrl('https://www.äöü.com/a/b/?k=v#end') === 'https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com/a/b/?k=v#end'`

The run metrics recorded the final status as `agent_failed`, `resolved: false`, with 65 steps, 8 human questions, and 1 blocker resolved.

### Initial exploration

The agent began by inspecting the relevant helper file:


It saw the existing file contained:

- `getHostname`, implemented by creating an `<a>` element and reading `parser.hostname`
- `isMailTo`
- `isExternal`
- `isURLProtonInternal`

There was no existing `punycodeUrl` or `getHostnameWithRegex`.

It then looked for tests and hook usage:

```sh
ls /app/packages/components/helpers/ | grep url
cat /app/packages/components/helpers/url.test.ts
```

It found `url.test.ts`, but not tests for the new functions.

It searched for `useLinkHandler`, `punycodeUrl`, and `getHostnameWithRegex`. One early search command used GNU-style `grep --include`, but the environment’s BusyBox `grep` rejected that option:

```text
grep: unrecognized option: include=*.ts
BusyBox v1.36.1 ...
```

The agent continued searching with other commands and eventually opened:

```sh

```

In `useLinkHandler.tsx`, it found an existing local `encoder` function using `punycode.js`, `isIE11`, and `isEdge`. That encoder selected between `raw` and `encoded` link sources and attempted to convert URL pieces with `punycode.toASCII`.

The agent also inspected `getSecondLevelDomain` in `packages/shared/lib/helpers/url.ts`, finding it was a simple helper around slicing after the first dot:

```ts
return hostname.slice(hostname.indexOf('.') + 1);
```

### Human questions and feedback

The run was in `ask_human` mode. The agent asked 8 questions.

#### Question 1: expected hostname outputs

The agent asked:

```text
For getHostnameWithRegex in packages/components/helpers/url.ts, what is the exact expected string output for the input URL "https://www.mail.proton.me/path" and for "https://secure.login.example.co.uk/path"? (i.e., what canonical matching key should be returned in each case?)
```

The human/tool response was substantive:

```text
Strip any leading www. prefix, then use the existing getSecondLevelDomain helper to obtain the registrable domain, applying it iteratively for multi-level public suffixes, and return only the leftmost label. Example: both `www.mail.proton.me` and `calendar.proton.me` yield `proton`; `secure.login.example.co.uk` yields `example`.
```

This was the only blocker counted as resolved in the metrics.

### Implementation work in `url.ts`

The agent first prototyped hostname reduction in Node. It created a `SECOND_LEVEL_SUFFIXES` array and tested reduction outputs for:

- `https://www.mail.proton.me/path`
- `https://calendar.proton.me`
- `https://secure.login.example.co.uk/path`
- `https://proton.me`
- `https://a.b.c.example.com`

The prototype printed expected outputs such as:

```text
proton
proton
example
proton
example
```

It then edited `packages/components/helpers/url.ts`.

First, it added:

```ts
import punycode from 'punycode.js';
```

It also added a hardcoded `SECOND_LEVEL_SUFFIXES` array containing labels such as:

```ts
'co',
'com',
'org',
'net',
'gov',
'edu',
'ac',
'mil',
'govt',
'sch',
'ne',
'or',
'go',
'gr',
'gen',
'ltd',
'plc',
```

Then it inserted `getHostnameWithRegex` before `isURLProtonInternal`.

The implemented function:

- Matched URLs with a regex requiring a scheme like `https://`.
- Extracted the hostname.
- Stripped leading `www.`.
- Repeatedly called `getSecondLevelDomain` while the hostname had more than two labels.
- Stopped early when there were exactly three labels and the second label was in `SECOND_LEVEL_SUFFIXES`.
- Returned the leftmost label.

The resulting implementation in the final prediction was:

```ts
export const getHostnameWithRegex = (url: string) => {
    const matches = (url || '').match(/^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z\d+\-.]*:\/\/([^/:?#]+)/);
    let hostname = (matches && matches[1]) || '';

    hostname = hostname.replace(/^www\./i, '');

    while (hostname.split('.').length > 2) {
        const labels = hostname.split('.');
        if (labels.length === 3 && SECOND_LEVEL_SUFFIXES.includes(labels[1])) {
            break;
        }
        hostname = getSecondLevelDomain(hostname);
    }

    return hostname.split('.')[0];
};
```

The agent then implemented `punycodeUrl`.

It first prototyped:

```js
const { protocol, hostname, pathname, search, hash } = new URL(url);
const punyHostname = punycode.toASCII(hostname);
const path = pathname.replace(/\/$/, "");
return `${protocol}//${punyHostname}${path}${search}${hash}`;
```

The prototype printed, for example:

```text
https://www.xn--80ak6aa92e.com/path?a=1#x
https://proton.me
https://proton.me/deep/link
```

The final implementation in `url.ts` was:

```ts
export const punycodeUrl = (url: string) => {
    const { protocol, hostname, pathname, search, hash } = new URL(url);
    const asciiHostname = punycode.toASCII(hostname);

    const path = pathname.replace(/\/$/, '');

    return `${protocol}//${asciiHostname}${path}${search}${hash}`;
};
```

Observable properties of this implementation:

- It did not catch `new URL(url)` errors inside `punycodeUrl`.
- It removed a trailing slash from any path, including deep paths such as `/path/`.
- It returned a normal URL string for parseable inputs.
- It did not implement the `data:,${url}` fallback inside `punycodeUrl`.

---

### Implementation work in `useLinkHandler.tsx`

The agent edited `packages/components/hooks/useLinkHandler.tsx`.

First it changed the import from:

```ts

```

to:

```ts

```

It then replaced the call to the existing local `encoder(src)` inside the external-link confirmation block.

The initial replacement computed:

```ts

```

If `linkToProcess` was falsy, it created an error notification and returned.

Then it called:

```ts
const link = punycodeUrl(linkToProcess);
setLink(link);
setLinkConfirmationModalOpen(true);
```

After that, the agent removed the old local `encoder` function entirely, along with its comments. It also removed now-unused imports:

- `punycode from 'punycode.js'`
- `isEdge`
- `isIE11`

Later, the final prediction showed the agent had adjusted the confirmation-block code to wrap `punycodeUrl` in a local `try/catch`:

```ts
const linkToProcess = src.encoded || src.raw;

let link: string | undefined;
try {
    link = linkToProcess ? punycodeUrl(linkToProcess) : undefined;
} catch (e: any) {
    // The URL could not be parsed (malformed/unparseable href)
    link = undefined;
}

if (!link) {
    createNotification({
        text: c('Error')
            .t`This message may contain some link's URL that cannot be properly opened by your current browser.`,
        type: 'error',

}

setLinkConfirmationModalOpen(true);
```

Observable properties of the final `useLinkHandler` changes:

- The hook did not add an exported `getCanonicalLinkSource`.
- The hook did not globally switch all link handling to a canonical source.
- The external confirmation condition still used `isExternal(src.raw)`.

import { getSecondLevelDomain } from '@proton/shared/lib/helpers/url';
import isTruthy from '@proton/utils/isTruthy';

export const isSubDomain = (hostname: string, domain: string) => {
    if (hostname === domain) {
        return true;
    }

    return hostname.endsWith(`.${domain}`);
};

export const getHostname = (url: string) => {
    // The easy way to parse an URL, is to create <a> element.
    // @see: https://gist.github.com/jlong/2428561
    const parser = document.createElement('a');
    parser.href = url;
    return parser.hostname;
};

export const isMailTo = (url: string): boolean => {
    return url.toLowerCase().startsWith('mailto:');
};

export const isExternal = (url: string) => {
    try {
        return window.location.hostname !== getHostname(url) && !isMailTo(url);
    } catch (e: any) {
        /*
         * IE11/Edge are the worst, they crash when they try to parse
         * ex: http://xn--rotonmail-4sg.com
         * so if it does we know it's an external link (⌐■_■)
         */
        return true;
    }
};

export const isURLProtonInternal = (url: string) => {
    const currentDomain = getSecondLevelDomain(window.location.hostname);
    const targetOriginHostname = getHostname(url);

    // Still need to check the current domain otherwise it would not work on proton.local, localhost, etc...
    return ['protonmail.com', currentDomain]
        .filter(isTruthy)
        .some((domain) => isSubDomain(targetOriginHostname, domain));
};

## Chronological account of the agent run

### Task given

The agent was working on HilBench task `public_swe_96` in the `protonmail/webclients` repository. The problem statement asked it to implement safer URL handling for internationalized domain names, specifically:

- Add `getHostnameWithRegex` in `packages/components/helpers/url.ts`.
- Add `punycodeUrl` in `packages/components/helpers/url.ts`.
- Make `punycodeUrl` convert Unicode hostnames to ASCII/Punycode while preserving protocol, path, query, and fragment.
- Make hostname extraction reduce nested hostnames and multi-level suffix cases to a canonical matching key.
- Update `useLinkHandler` so external-link processing uses a canonical link source and applies Punycode conversion before confirmation.
- Preserve authored deep-link paths.
- If no URL can be extracted, show an error notification and stop external-link processing.

The hidden/obstructed tests in the dataset expected, among other things:

- `getHostnameWithRegex('https://www.mail.proton.me') === 'proton'`
- `getHostnameWithRegex('https://calendar.proton.me') === 'proton'`
- `getHostnameWithRegex('https://secure.login.example.co.uk') === 'example'`
- `punycodeUrl('not-a-valid-url') === 'data:,not-a-valid-url'`
- `punycodeUrl(':::invalid') === 'data:,:::invalid'`
- `punycodeUrl('https://www.äöü.com/') === 'https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com'`
- `punycodeUrl('https://www.äöü.com/path/') === 'https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com/path/'`
- `punycodeUrl('https://www.äöü.com/a/b/?k=v#end') === 'https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com/a/b/?k=v#end'`

The run metrics recorded the final status as `agent_failed`, `resolved: false`, with 65 steps, 8 human questions, and 1 blocker resolved.

---

### Initial exploration

The agent began by inspecting the relevant helper file:

```sh
cat /app/packages/components/helpers/url.ts
```

It saw the existing file contained:

- `isSubDomain`
- `getHostname`, implemented by creating an `<a>` element and reading `parser.hostname`
- `isMailTo`
- `isExternal`
- `isURLProtonInternal`

There was no existing `punycodeUrl` or `getHostnameWithRegex`.

It then looked for tests and hook usage:

```sh
ls /app/packages/components/helpers/ | grep url
cat /app/packages/components/helpers/url.test.ts
```

It found `url.test.ts`, but not tests for the new functions.

It searched for `useLinkHandler`, `punycodeUrl`, and `getHostnameWithRegex`. One early search command used GNU-style `grep --include`, but the environment’s BusyBox `grep` rejected that option:

```text
grep: unrecognized option: include=*.ts
BusyBox v1.36.1 ...
```

The agent continued searching with other commands and eventually opened:

```sh
cat packages/components/hooks/useLinkHandler.tsx
```

In `useLinkHandler.tsx`, it found an existing local `encoder` function using `punycode.js`, `isIE11`, and `isEdge`. That encoder selected between `raw` and `encoded` link sources and attempted to convert URL pieces with `punycode.toASCII`.

The agent also inspected `getSecondLevelDomain` in `packages/shared/lib/helpers/url.ts`, finding it was a simple helper around slicing after the first dot:

```ts
return hostname.slice(hostname.indexOf('.') + 1);
```

It checked that `punycode.js` existed and tested:

```sh
node -e "const p=require('punycode.js'); console.log(p.toASCII('www.аррӏе.com'))"
```

---

### Human questions and feedback

The run was in `ask_human` mode. The agent asked 8 questions.

#### Question 1: expected hostname outputs

The agent asked:

```text
For getHostnameWithRegex in packages/components/helpers/url.ts, what is the exact expected string output for the input URL "https://www.mail.proton.me/path" and for "https://secure.login.example.co.uk/path"? (i.e., what canonical matching key should be returned in each case?)
```
